t: A state of Czechs and Slovaks created from the ruins of Austria-Hungary in 1918, with Prague as its capital.
Its interwar democracy was the only one in Central Europe to last until the Munich Agreement of 1938 dismembered it.
After 1948 it was a communist state of the Soviet bloc; the Velvet Revolution of 1989 led to its peaceful division in 1992.
dyk: The British Bren light machine gun was developed from the Czechoslovak ZB vz. 26; its name joins Brno, where it was designed, and Enfield, where it was made.
ev: Independence proclaimed in Prague on 28 October; Masaryk becomes president
The Munich Agreement forces the cession of the Sudetenland to Germany
Germany occupies Bohemia and Moravia; Slovakia becomes a separate state
The Communist Party seizes full power in February
Warsaw Pact armies invade to end the Prague Spring
The Velvet Revolution ends communist rule; Václav Havel becomes president
The federation is dissolved peacefully on 31 December
